titel: The Moon Could Become a Radio Sanctuary for Astronomy

einzeiler: Scientists propose a radio telescope on the Moon's far side to escape Earth's noise.
kurzfassung: Earth has become electromagnetically deafening and its upper atmosphere blocks low frequency signals, hiding the cosmos from terrestrial telescopes. To overcome this, researchers propose building LFT3, a radio telescope on the far side of the Moon. However, this radio sanctuary faces a strict deadline because upcoming lunar exploration threatens to permanently fill the far side with noise by 2030.
stichpunkte: Earth's heavy reliance on satellites, radar, and wireless networks creates massive radio frequency interference.
The ionosphere acts as a plasma mirror, blocking low frequency radio waves from reaching ground-based telescopes.
The far side of the Moon is shielded by thousands of miles of solid rock, offering a pristine radio-quiet environment.
Upcoming lunar missions and infrastructure threaten to permanently destroy this radio silence by 2030.
Scientists propose LFT3, a low-cost radio antenna array deployed directly onto the lunar regolith.
Utilizing commercial lunar landers keeps the mission budget at an estimated 150 million dollars.
An onboard radiation-hardened AI system must filter data locally due to a strict lunar data bottleneck.
The telescope's primary goals include searching for technosignatures, exoplanetary auroras, and fast radio bursts.

clips.hook: The mysterious frequency of the Wow signal
clips.text: The famous signal was detected at fourteen hundred and twenty megahertz, matching the natural emission frequency of neutral hydrogen atoms.

clips.hook: Two thousand miles of solid rock as a shield
clips.text: The massive bulk of the Moon blocks all human-made terrestrial interference, creating the quietest location in the inner solar system.

clips.hook: Building a lunar observatory for one hundred and fifty million
clips.text: While flagship space telescopes cost billions of years and dollars, this proposed mission achieves a lean budget by utilizing commercial payload services.

clips.hook: An onboard democracy to survive cosmic rays
clips.text: To prevent radiation from corrupting calculations, the system runs identical operations across three circuits and uses a voting mechanism to overrule errors.

clips.hook: Is the great silence just a temporary phase?
clips.text: Civilizations might routinely deafen themselves with their own technological progress shortly after inventing radio, leaving only those who build instruments on their moons able to listen.

beschreibung:
Scientists are proposing LFT3, a radio telescope on the far side of the Moon that could escape Earth’s radio interference and search for faint signals such as alien technosignatures and exoplanetary auroras.

Researchers argue the mission should be deployed before growing lunar activity contaminates this uniquely quiet environment.
